description: We are high schoolers interested in using our code to change the world.
summary: We developed a simple, 2D game to help kids age 7-12 learn about space exploration. They learn how to manage oxygen and navigate their way through space. In space, times are tough, so that's exactly what we teach. The brute force of nature is taught in a fun, accessible way so all inspiring astronauts can learn. In the game, there are three game modes; each game mode is different so no matter what your play style is, you can have a blast while learning.
details:
When coming up for "Lunaria", we had to make some crucial decisions.

Very early on, we decided for a 2D style game where all students can enjoy a simple, fun website to learn about deep exploration. Our project is a website, derived from an HTML file.

It's deployed using Vercel, and was coded with the assistance of SI to broaden our technical skills with newer coding tools.

We aim to benefit young children interested in space, so their is equitable access into the industry. Our impact is similar, we provide fair and equitable tools so every student can one day become an astronaut. As for our tech stack:

Core Technologies 

  • HTML5 - page structure and game UI
  • CSS3 - styling, animations, and visual effects
  • JavaScript - game logic and interactions
  • Vercel - Deploying the website
  • Web Audio API - Sound and audio

AI tools 

  • Chat GPT & Gemini - assisted with research, game concept development, and problem-solving
  • Claude/Claude Code - assisted with code generation and debugging

Our project aims to provide a new, creative way to address this problem. We wanted to take already existing game ideas and alter them to be space related, so children are familiar and can get right into playing.

When building, our protocol was to first research, then look for UI, then build. We considered the accessibility, the look, and how the user experience is.
